description: Shared base HTTP GET used by every client (SteamSpyClient, SteamStoreClient, SteamReviewsClient): session reuse, per-request timeout, a custom User-Agent identifying the tool, exponential backoff with jitter, and bounded retries. Returns (status_code, payload) rather than raising on 4xx/5xx so the caller can persist the failure verbatim (ADR-005, ADR-003).
signature: def get_json(self, url: str, params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> tuple[int, dict]
docstring:
Perform a rate-limited-by-caller HTTP GET and parse the JSON body.

Args:
    url: Absolute request URL.
    params: Query parameters.

Returns:
    (status_code, payload). payload is the parsed JSON dict on any status where the body is valid JSON (including 4xx/5xx error bodies that happen to be JSON, e.g. SteamSpy's undocumented error shapes). If the body is not valid JSON (e.g. an HTML error page), payload is {'_raw_text': <body text>, '_parse_error': True} so the caller can still persist something and mark the fetch failed, per the acquisition module's edge case for non-JSON responses.

Retries:
    On a connection error, timeout, or 5xx status, retries up to AcquisitionConfig.max_retries times with exponential backoff (base backoff_base_seconds, capped at backoff_max_seconds) plus random jitter, before returning the final attempt's outcome. This method does not itself call RateLimiter.acquire() -- callers (SteamSpyClient, SteamStoreClient, SteamReviewsClient) are responsible for calling acquire() once per logical request before invoking get_json, so that retries internal to get_json do not each separately re-throttle against the token bucket.
preconditions: url is an absolute http(s) URL
postconditions: Always returns a (int, dict) tuple; never raises for a well-formed url except for programmer-error cases (e.g. a malformed URL string)
On success, status_code is the status of the LAST attempt made, and payload is that attempt's parsed (or raw-text-wrapped) body
Retries never exceed max_retries additional attempts beyond the first

edge_cases.input: Server returns 200 with a non-JSON body (HTML)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns (200, {'_raw_text': ..., '_parse_error': True}); still a tuple, no exception

edge_cases.input: Connection timeout on every attempt up to max_retries
edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns the final attempt's outcome, typically (0, {'_raw_text': '', '_parse_error': True, '_transport_error': 'timeout'}) using a sentinel status_code=0 to represent 'no HTTP response received at all', distinct from any real status code

edge_cases.input: Server returns 500 on the first attempt, 200 on the retry
edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns (200, <parsed body>) -- only the final attempt's outcome matters
returned as-is, (429, <parsed body or raw text>); RateLimiter.observe_response (called by the higher-level client, not by get_json) is what reacts to 429, not get_json itself

unit_tests.name: test_success_returns_parsed_json
unit_tests.description: A 200 response with a valid JSON body returns (200, <dict>).

unit_tests.name: test_non_json_body_wrapped
unit_tests.description: A 200 response with an HTML body returns the raw-text wrapper with _parse_error=True.

unit_tests.name: test_retries_on_5xx_then_succeeds
unit_tests.description: A mocked transport returning 500 then 200 results in the 200 outcome, using exactly 2 attempts.

unit_tests.name: test_exhausts_retries_on_persistent_5xx
unit_tests.description: A transport always returning 503 makes exactly max_retries+1 attempts and returns the last (503, ...).

unit_tests.name: test_timeout_returns_sentinel_status
unit_tests.description: A transport that always raises a timeout returns status_code=0 with a transport-error marker.
